clue.text: A white pawn

definitions.meaning: a German white wine from the Rhineland, named in Britain after the town of Hochheim
to pawn something is to deposit it with a pawnbroker as security for a loan

explanation.surface: A chess player picks out a light-coloured pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue had a stray '77' from the OCR; the page reads 'A white pawn'. 'White' looks like the chess side but is a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is the traditional British name for German white wine, and also slang for pawning goods.

clue.text: Suffering from condition no in-patient has?

definitions.text: Suffering from condition no in-patient has?

parts.words: Suffering from condition no in-patient has?
parts.note: a patient kept in hospital cannot be ill at home, so their state is never being ill in that place

explanation.surface: A medical riddle about an illness that hospital patients never get.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue split in-patient badly; the page reads 'no in-patient'. Read the answer's halves literally: ill in one's own house.
explanation.definitionFit: Being homesick is pining for home, a condition here read as being sick at home.

clue.text: Keeps under control, having organized sanction

indicators.note: something organized has been arranged, so these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A body brings a problem into line by arranging penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain something is to hold it in check, keeping it under control.

clue.text: What sounds like appropriate talent produces something worthless

indicators.note: these words say the next word is to be heard rather than spelt, giving a written form with a silent first letter

parts.note: to appropriate is to steal, which in British slang is to nick
a knack is a natural talent or skill

explanation.surface: Stealing someone's gifts only yields rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A knick-knack is a small trinket or ornament of little value.

clue.text: Shark in harbour

definitions.meaning: the ... shark is a slow, bottom-dwelling species
to harbour a feeling, such as a grudge

explanation.surface: A shark lurks in the port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbour' looks like a place but is a verb: to cherish a feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The nurse shark is a species, and to nurse a grievance is to harbour it.

clue.text: Protest that produces ill-feeling

definitions.meaning: literally a feeling of being ill, an ailment or disorder

explanation.surface: A grievance breeds resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-feeling' suggests resentment; read literally it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is both an objection and a medical ailment.

clue.text: Capacity for work masses still don't have

definitions.meaning: in physics, energy is the capacity to do work
a body at rest has no energy of motion

explanation.surface: Ordinary people still lack the ability to toil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masses' suggests crowds of people; it means physical bodies, and 'still' means motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion, possessed by moving bodies and absent from stationary ones.

clue.text: Declared a short volume outstanding

parts.note: V is the short form for volume
a debt outstanding is owed

explanation.surface: Someone announced a slim book was a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' suggests excellent; it means still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Avowed means openly declared or admitted.

clue.text: Citizen of divided country in East engaged in religious work

indicators.note: the letter is set into the other word, held within it

parts.note: the Koran is the holy book of Islam

explanation.surface: A national of a split country takes up missionary work in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Korea has been split into North and South since 1945, so a Korean is a citizen of a divided country.

clue.text: European city's Irish quarter?

definitions.meaning: ... is a city in north-west Germany
Ireland has four historic provinces, so each province is a quarter of the island

explanation.surface: A city's district where the Irish live.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'quarter' is not a city district but one of Ireland's four provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: Münster is a German city, and Munster is one of the four traditional provinces of Ireland.

clue.text: Strong pressure to vote here help win it corruptly

indicators.note: letters treated corruptly are tampered with, rearranged out of their original order

explanation.surface: A party boss says the vote must be won here, by foul means if needed.
explanation.walkthrough: A three-line whip is the strictest instruction from a British party's whips, its importance once marked by underlining three times.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-line whip is a strict order to party MPs to attend and vote as instructed.

clue.text: Parts of this work unit may be said to come together

definitions.text: Parts of this work unit may be said to come together

parts.words: Parts of this work unit may be said to come together
parts.note: the proverb 'cometh the hour, cometh the man' says a person and a moment arrive together, and those are the two halves of a labour unit

explanation.surface: Components of a team are assembled in one place.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'cometh the hour, cometh the man' means the right person appears when needed; its two nouns are the parts of the work unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-hour is a unit of labour: the work one person does in sixty minutes.

clue.text: Said to look fixedly and carefully where flight is located

indicators.note: this word marks the following piece as spoken, so its sound is kept and its spelling changed

parts.note: to stare is to look fixedly
to do something well is to do it carefully and properly

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep a sharp eye on the airport departures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests an aeroplane, but here it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the vertical shaft in a building that houses a staircase, or flight of steps.

clue.text: Leading character from Greek theatre

parts.note: the opening sound of the word theatre, th, is written in Greek with a single letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The star of an ancient Athenian play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading character' suggests a protagonist; it is the first letter, in Greek, of the word for theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, the one that begins the Greek word theatron.

clue.text: Study spiel about winner, surely in state of readiness

indicators.note: the outer pair of pieces goes around the next piece, so it lies between them

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a pitch is a salesman's spiel
a cert is a racing certainty, a horse sure to win

explanation.surface: A tipster's patter about a sure-fire winner leaves the punter ready to bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a room but is the old verb con, to learn; 'winner, surely' is racing slang for a horse certain to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Concert pitch is the standard tuning for instruments, and figuratively a state of full readiness.

clue.text: Articles about sultan's subject showing a kind of madness

indicators.note: the first pieces surround the second, which sits within them

parts.note: the and a are the definite and indefinite articles
Oman is ruled by a sultan, so an Omani is a sultan's subject

explanation.surface: Writings about a ruler's people reveal a strange madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests pieces of writing; they are the grammatical words the and a. Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: Theomania is a mania in which a person believes they are God, a form of madness.

clue.text: In silence going round home? Precisely

indicators.note: the first word surrounds the second, putting it inside

parts.note: mutely means silently
in can mean at home

explanation.surface: Someone silently circles the house with great care.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutely means in fine detail, precisely.

clue.text: We are prone to accept blow as pardonable offence

indicators.note: one word takes another in, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
a hit is a blow
to lie is to be prone, flat

explanation.surface: Some people are apt to take a punch as a forgivable sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone' suggests inclined to; it means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A white lie is a harmless untruth told to spare feelings, a forgivable offence.

clue.text: Badly lit den that is typical of amateurs

indicators.note: something done badly is done wrong, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A poorly lit room is the mark of the amateur decorator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges the letters of LIT DEN and THAT IS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante is a dabbler or amateur, so dilettantish describes amateurish behaviour.

clue.text: Fare from Asia, passing over cold Northern sea

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece goes above the other, so it comes first

parts.note: a balti is a spicy dish of Pakistani origin, popular in British curry houses

explanation.surface: A traveller's ticket from Asia takes them across a chilly northern sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket; it is food, a balti curry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic is a sea in northern Europe.

clue.text: Animal found in jungle, primarily — one keeping watch endlessly

indicators.note: this word picks out the first letter of the word beside it

parts.note: one is the indefinite article a

indicators.note: the last letter is taken away from the piece

parts.note: to guard is to keep watch

explanation.surface: A creature in the jungle stands sentry without rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the final D from GUARD, leaving GUAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaguar is a big cat of Central and South America.

clue.text: Knowing peace at last after a period of conflict

parts.note: a war is a period of armed conflict

indicators.note: these words point to the final letter of the word before them

explanation.surface: Wisdom only comes after the fighting is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the last letter of peace behind A and WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aware is to be knowing, conscious of something.

clue.text: Hearts united, say, in notable courtship

definitions.text: Hearts united, say, in notable courtship

parts.words: Hearts united, say, in notable courtship
parts.note: two lovers' hearts joined in a celebrated wooing, read in card terms as hearts being one of the higher-ranking suits

explanation.surface: A famous romance ends with two hearts joined.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, hearts and spades are the senior suits; a suit is also a wooing, so a notable one is a big romance.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a major suit is hearts or spades, the two higher-scoring suits.

clue.text: Mason accepting good rule

indicators.note: one word takes in the other, which ends up inside

parts.note: Jude Fawley, hero of Hardy's Jude the Obscure, is a stonemason

explanation.surface: A Freemason takes on a virtuous principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mason' suggests a Freemason; it is Hardy's stonemason hero Jude.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge is to rule, as a court rules on a matter.

clue.text: Increase stiffness of test, initially bad enough

indicators.note: this word picks out the first letter of the word before it
a bad version of the next word is a scrambled one, its letters out of order

explanation.surface: A tough exam is just bad enough to stiffen a student's resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges ENOUGH into OUGHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To toughen something is to make it harder or stiffer.

clue.text: Source of power a prisoner's more comfortable with

definitions.meaning: a battery that uses a paste rather than a liquid electrolyte
a prison cell that is not damp would be easier to live in

explanation.surface: A prisoner wants a cell that powers things or keeps them comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading treats the two words literally: a cell that is not wet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry cell is a battery type, and also, taken literally, a prison room free of damp.

clue.text: Eccentric actor who gets a hand?

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
a player is an actor

explanation.surface: An offbeat performer wins applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets a hand' suggests applause; a card player is dealt a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A card player is someone dealt a hand of cards in a game.

clue.text: Third of herd housed in extra cowshed

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the other word, as if lodged within it

parts.note: a bye is an extra in cricket, a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball

indicators.note: these words pick the third letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cow from the herd is kept in a spare shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third of herd' suggests a fraction of the cattle; it is the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed, chiefly in Scotland and northern England.
